topic: Roles of Organisms in Biogeochemical Cycles
key_concepts: Biogeochemical cycles involve both biotic and abiotic components.
Water cycle includes evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, and runoff.
Plants release water vapor through stomata during transpiration.
Animals add water vapor through breathing, perspiration, and urination.
Photosynthesis takes in carbon dioxide and releases oxygen.
Cellular respiration uses oxygen to produce energy.
Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia.
Rhizobium and other nitrogen-fixing bacteria live in soil or legume root nodules.
Nitrification converts ammonia into nitrates or nitrites plants can absorb.
Plants assimilate nitrates to make proteins and nucleic acids.
Animals obtain nitrogen by eating plants.
Decomposers and denitrifying bacteria return nitrogen to soil and atmosphere.
